problem: ROS lacks direct support for learning-based RL agents, and Gazebo is neither photorealistic nor fast enough for vision-based agents. Habitat, in turn, has no ROS bridge and cannot simulate its discrete-action agents with physics.
motivation: Roboticists want to train in fast photorealistic simulators and then embody the agents on robots through ROS. They also want to test classical ROS planners in photorealistic scanned scenes. A bridge is only useful if it adds negligible performance loss and acceptable runtime overhead.
key_idea: ros_x_habitat is a ROS package that connects Habitat Sim v2 with ROS agents and simulators, and converts discrete Habitat actions into velocity commands so they run under physics.
insight: Agents trained fast without physics and with discrete actions still work reasonably under continuous physics: mean SPL drops only from 0.495 to 0.455. Physics costs about 8x runtime, so it can be reserved for validation or testing. ROS adds no change in navigation results (identical step counts per episode) but adds 5x runtime without physics and under 20% with physics.
method: Package architecture: a ROS Noetic Python package of nodes, topics and services, with an env_node wrapping the Habitat environment and an agent node that can be swapped for a ROS planner.
Mode (a): a Habitat RL agent runs in Habitat Sim v2 through ROS, with or without physics, as a regression test of the interface.

Mode (b): a ROS planner (move_base with rtabmap mapping) runs in physics-enabled Habitat Sim v2 on Matterport3D scenes; depth is converted to laser scans via depthimage_to_laserscan and a prebuilt 2D occupancy map is provided.
Mode (c): a Habitat RGBD agent runs in Gazebo (turtlebot3 House scene) through the ROS topics.

Discrete-to-continuous action mapping (Algorithm 1): each action becomes a velocity (0.25 m or 10° divided by a 1 s control period), applied for 60 physics steps per second via step_physics(), using the LoCoBot asset.

setting.backbone: Habitat v2 PointGoal RGBD agent (pretrained RL, frozen, not retrained); move_base and rtabmap for the classical demo
setting.training_data: none (uses pretrained Habitat v2 agent trained without physics on Matterport3D-style Habitat data)
setting.observation: RGB-D plus PointGoal (GPS/compass); depth emulated as laser scan for ROS planners
setting.action_space: discrete move_forward 0.25 m / turn 10° / stop, mapped to continuous velocity commands under physics
setting.simulator: Habitat Sim v2 (with Bullet physics) and Gazebo
setting.privileged: prebuilt 2D occupancy map and manually set goal for the ROS planner demo; PointGoal coordinates for the agent

numbers.method: Habitat v2 RGBD agent, -Physics (discrete, with or without ROS)
numbers.extra: no physics; ROS gives identical results
numbers.evidence: Fig. 2 caption: mean spl produced by the v2 RGBD agent is 0.495 without physics

numbers.method: Habitat v2 RGBD agent via ros_x_habitat, +Physics
numbers.extra: discrete actions mapped to velocities, LoCoBot asset, physics on
numbers.evidence: Fig. 2 caption: spl dropped slightly to 0.455 after physics was enabled

numbers_note: Only SPL means from figure captions; runtime results given only as figure and text (8x with physics, 5x with ROS, over 274,000 steps in under 30 h). No quantitative metrics for the planner or Gazebo demos.
results: Physics lowers mean SPL from 0.495 to 0.455 (129 more failed episodes, 80 of them stuck), and ROS does not change navigation outcomes. Total runtime grows about 8x with physics, and ROS adds about 5x without physics and under 20% with physics. The full setup still runs at over 2x real time. The move_base demos succeeded in one of two Matterport scenes, and the Habitat agent succeeded in two of three Gazebo episodes.
limitations: Only qualitative demos for the ROS planner and Gazebo modes, with no quantitative metrics; no physical robot deployment.
Planar velocity mapping cannot climb stairs, which causes stuck failures, and physics slows simulation about 8x.
Evaluated only on PointGoal navigation with one agent, and ROS planner localization is weak in clutter.
